A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Orchid and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The shared methods and experiments can be matched despite rewriting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B-C report original depth and normal benchmarks, ablations, generated images, and joint inpainting results.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by runtime measurements, a human preference study, latent-space PCA, and additional comparisons.

M1.justification: The joint VAE, latent diffusion model, color-conditioned finetuning, and RePaint-style joint inpainting procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 specifies the already-used distillation loss more explicitly; this does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluation coverage remain the same, including COCO-caption generation, zero-shot depth and normal prediction, and joint inpainting. The new preference study, timing measurements, and PCA examine existing tasks or representations rather than introducing new model tasks or data domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds an SDXL-inpainting, Marigold-DC, and Lotus-normal pipeline to Figures 9 and 21-22, where v1 showed Orchid alone. It adds DepthAnything-v2 plus DSINE to Table 4, revises comparator participation in Figures 6, 7, and 13, and adds quantitative and preference comparisons against the pretrained RGB LDM in Table 8.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include single-H100 timing, aesthetics and text-adherence ratings from 40 users viewing 25 images each, and PCA on 1,000 concatenated depth-normal latent samples. Ablation reporting drops FID, AbsRel, and mean angular error. The previously stated main benchmark settings and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing joint-latent, distillation, and pseudo-label ablations are extended with additional geometry outcomes in Table 5. v2 adds a PCA check of depth-normal redundancy and comparative inpainting failure cases. The VAE-only pseudo-label reconstruction improvements reported in v1 Section 4.5 are no longer reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new preference percentages and PCA explained variance are descriptive findings rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2-3 and the existing Table 4 scores are unchanged. v2 adds DepthAnything-v2 plus DSINE inconsistency scores of 0.059 on NYUv2 and 0.144 on KITTI, runtime results, additional ablation outcomes, PCA findings, and inpainting comparisons. Table 8 reports Orchid preference rates of 47.4% for aesthetics and 46.9% for text adherence. Some earlier ablation entries disappear, including FID values of 18.74 for joint and 17.11 for disentangled latents.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the existing distillation loss as a weighted L1 distance between teacher and student latent means. v1 referenced this loss without defining it. The other mathematical formulations remain substantially unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains unified appearance-geometry generation with the same downstream capabilities. v2 extends the main claims to qualitatively better inpainting than multi-step alternatives and lower memory consumption; v1 emphasized plausible joint inpainting, speed, and consistency.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations and qualifications: unbounded inverse depth is linked to long-range accuracy, range-limited ground truth is identified as a benchmark limitation, and Appendix F identifies oversmoothing on grass, fur, and hair. It also qualifies RGB quality by the pretrained model, explains excluded runtime I/O, and discloses that the inpainting baseline predicts normals without conditioning on observed normals.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses distillation and KL weights of 10^-6 and 10^-3, the discriminator architecture, stage-specific dataset sampling, and filtering of examples with teacher disagreement. These improve documentation of existing training; the PDFs do not establish that these procedures were newly introduced in v2.

R1.justification: Related work substantially refocuses its inverse-problem discussion toward 3D completion, editing, and geometric diffusion priors, adding works such as Reffusion, NeRFiller, RealmDreamer, and Marigold-DC while removing several earlier references. v2 also explicitly distinguishes Orchid from GeoWizard's separate representations and from systems combining multiple appearance and geometry priors.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with substantial revisions to related work and explanatory prose. Ablations are reorganized into the main text, and the appendix is restructured into sections covering runtime, ablation details, color quality, qualitative results, and limitations.

P2.justification: Figure 9 becomes a full-width baseline comparison, and the original Figure 21 is rearranged across Figures 21-22 with comparator panels. Figures 5-7 and 13 are revised, Table 4 gains a comparator column, the ablation table is relocated and restructured, and runtime and user-study tables are added.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked measured runtime and direct inpainting baselines, leaving important practical advantages of the joint model insufficiently tested. v2 addresses these gaps through Table 7 and Figures 9 and 21-22, while Table 8 evaluates preservation of RGB generation quality. Additional training details and explicit limitations further strengthen the paper. Removing some ablation metrics reduces completeness, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the new evidence substantially improves support for the central contribution.
